name: Nuclear plant safety
value: ZNPP on one line after 8 Nov power cut
summary: Zaporizhzhia relies on a single power line after losing off-site power on 8 Nov; IAEA warns on Ukraine's winter grid
state: Zaporizhzhia lost off-site power on 8 Nov and ran on emergency diesel generators, according to its Russian-installed management (US News, citing Reuters); it now relies on a single 330kV line (ANS, 19 Nov). IAEA Director General Grossi told the IAEA Board on 18 Nov that it would be difficult to overstate his concern about Ukraine's grid as winter sets in. No damage to safety-critical systems, INES level 2 event or radiological release was found as of 23 Nov.
for_you: There is no radiological risk to the public reported. The IAEA publishes regular updates on Ukrainian nuclear plants; follow national authorities' guidance if travelling in Ukraine, including FCDO travel advice.
rubric_hit: Off-site power loss and IAEA concern over grid = Watch; no safety-system damage

sources.title: ANS Nuclear Newswire — IAEA, Grossi give updates on Ukraine, Iran, North Korea
US News — Zaporizhzhia nuclear plant relying on generators again after losing external power

why: Fighting near nuclear power plants risks a radiological release; the IAEA reports on Zaporizhzhia and other plants in or near war zones.
drivers: Off-site power losses, strikes near plants, staffing, cooling water, military occupation.

rubric.alert: Damage to safety-critical systems, an INES level 2 or higher event, or a radiological release.
rubric.watch: A plant loses all off-site power, strikes land near a plant, or the IAEA reports a deteriorating safety situation.
rubric.normal: No new IAEA safety concerns at plants in or near conflict zones.
